purpose: Baseline ('before' refinements) shape/timing comparison of the full-AOI Ian solver's own domain-boundary outflow against the real NWIS 02263800 gauge record. NOT a magnitude comparison -- gauge 02263800's watershed (231 km^2) is ~44x this AOI's own area (5.24 km^2); see CLAUDE.md's 2026-07-23/24 entry.

observed_gauge_02263800.note: daily-resolution record -- exact time-of-day within Sep 30 not resolvable

interpretation: Our AOI's own boundary-outflow response lags its own rain peak by only 1.3 hours, vs. the real gauge's ~24-hour lag between rain peak and flow peak. This is the expected direction and rough order of magnitude for the watershed-scale mismatch already identified: a small (5.24 km^2) headwater patch has a short internal flow path and near-immediate runoff response, while the real gauge integrates routing/storage delay across the full 231 km^2 watershed. This is NOT necessarily evidence the local physics (Manning's n, infiltration, mesh routing) is wrong -- it's a structural consequence of comparing a small sub-catchment's own edge-outflow timing to a much larger integrated watershed's outlet timing. A genuinely apples-to-apples timing check would need either explicit downstream routing (unit hydrograph / Muskingum convolution) from this AOI to the gauge, or a new test site built at a gauge whose watershed is actually AOI-scale (Lance's original 'reconstruct a real flood' ask).
next_step: Re-run this same comparison after the planned physics refinements (soil-type infiltration, graded impervious, engineered pond outlet) land, to see whether they measurably change this AOI-internal lag -- even without solving the watershed-scale mismatch itself, that's a legitimate before/after check that the refinements are doing something physically real.

after_refinements.note: Full-AOI Ian solver only (site1/site2 mesh solver has no external gauge to compare against -- see the watershed-area-mismatch reasoning). Reflects NLCD graded impervious added on top of the pre-existing per-cell SSURGO Horton (already spatially-varying before this session). Pond-outlet-control and SFWMD/FDOT changes do not apply to this grid-based full-AOI solver.
